gen-dafont-plakkaat-general-sans: General Sans moves along at a steady pressure, its plain sans letters open at every bend. General Sans would make Plakkaat's heavy, nearly closed curls look cramped if the heading were shrunk small.
gen-dafont-quantum-manrope: Quantum spreads its letters loosely with a compressed ascender, giving headings a techy lightness. Manrope keeps the curved mouths bright and the line at one width, which suits text.
gen-dafont-redux-switzer: Wiry and approachable, Switzer is built from tubular strokes that all end at the same measured thickness. Switzer carries a text block smoothly, while Redux's wide spacing and varied stroke weight stay in the heading.
gen-dafont-starborn-work-sans: Work Sans skims along with strokes that never change weight, and its tall mean line keeps things modern. Starborn's dreamy gaps sit above it.
gen-dafont-stencilia-fs-fira-sans: Stencilia is structural and striking, with spacious gaps at its curve terminals. Fira Sans follows with a larger-than-usual x-height and wide-open s curves, so a long page of plain sans text feels drawn with a single tip and stays effortless to follow.
gen-dafont-stentiga-fs-epilogue: Crossbars as thick as the stems and tracking opened wide give Stentiga its refined, luxurious stretch. Epilogue's curvy, wire-like monoline lowercase reads loose and friendly.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-supreme: Visitor pulls every stroke at a single width, like solder through a nozzle, with gaping mouths on the e. Supreme's crisp plain sans keeps its letters held open, so a long page of text feels steady and unhurried.
gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-public-sans: Woodgod's lowercase climbs nearly to the capitals, vintage and commanding. Public Sans answers with a hefty body and broad open counters, making this sans-serif pairing feel sturdy and trustworthy.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-archivo: Archivo reads like an editorial sans-serif, its curves opening outward and its tall x-height holding firm. Alien Encounters adds big gaps and an otherworldly lift on top.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-asap: Azonix holds its stroke at fixed pressure, capitals barely above lowercase, authoritative and crisp even when shrunk. Asap reads as open arcs with a body height near the capitals, so a long sans-serif page flows readily.
